copy_pick.why: Its clipped 'EXPLOSIONS OVER THE NEVA, PHONES RAISED' wears the field-notes directive, and 'a bad night and a free pass at once' lands the sharp contrast without the 'which is a bold/strange way to' closer that Candidate 1 recycles or Candidate 2's 'because even the yogurt isn't safe'-style tag.

doom.driver: St Petersburg under attack from Ukrainian drone swarm. Video posted on social media shows multiple explosions in St Petersburg, Russia after a suspected Ukrainian drone swarm.
doom.blurb: EXPLOSIONS OVER THE NEVA, PHONES RAISED
doom.summary: A Ukrainian drone swarm lit up St Petersburg on the same day Trump put the Graham Act sanctions on ice, so Moscow gets a bad night and a free pass at once. Meanwhile, a mystery 'incident' killed people at one of Canada's busiest military bases, France logged 1,200 arrests, and Tirana fought its riot police. On the AI front, DeepSeek shipped another model and OpenCode leaked user credentials, which is about as calm as that beat gets.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: DeepSeek v4.1 Flash dropped to heavy developer interest, another steady step rather than a leap.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: Trump waived congressionally mandated Russia sanctions two days before they took effect, while Canada's planned surveillance law adds to pressure on encryption.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Drone strikes on Russia's second city, unresolved Iran-US hostility and settlers attacking European diplomats keep several fronts hot.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: Websites are barring AI agents and the OpenCode credential leak shows how brittle the agent-tooling ecosystem remains.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: An unexplained deadly fire at CFB Wainwright, plus cost-of-living riots spreading across France and Albania, adds a lot of volatility.

doom.dalle_prompt:
Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. A weather-dominated night panorama of St Petersburg on the flat Neva delta, the whole city seen through a thick, low blanket of smoke-laden fog and drizzle rolling in off the Gulf of Finland. The haze glows blood orange from below, as if volcanic underlighting is bleeding up through the mist. Cool tones are nearly extinguished, leaving only deep soot black and molten orange. Dim fireball flashes bloom inside the fog along the far horizon, each one a soft blown-out orange halo with no hard edges. Thick black smoke columns rise into the murk and catch the glow from beneath. The wide Neva fills the middle of the frame, a black mirror streaked with smeared orange reflections and pocked by rain rings.

Elements, all half-swallowed by the haze:
1. The gilded Admiralty needle-spire and the dark dome of St Isaac's Cathedral as small silhouettes with faint orange rim light on the left of the skyline.
2. The twisting glass spire of the Lakhta Center far on the right, its tip vanishing into the glowing fog, backlit by a fireball.
3. A swarm of small pale delta-wing drones, drawn as tiny dark crosses and triangles, crossing the smoky sky in a loose V, a few trailing orange sparks.
4. Thin dotted orange tracer arcs rising into the cloud base, fading as they climb.
5. In the foreground, the dark frame of a high Soviet apartment block window and balcony, with a small group of whole silhouetted residents in coats standing frozen and holding up phones. The phones are tiny glowing amber rectangles, and the rain streaks the glass.

The foreground is crushed to near-black, the midground is a wall of orange-lit fog, and the distance dissolves into ember-colored haze. The mood is eerie, hushed and uncanny.

minor: The glowing phones at the far left (~215,695) and center-left (~360,737) sit above very dark, vague shapes. The hands and arms holding them are barely visible, so the phones look slightly floating.
The foreground people are crushed to near-black blobs, and some of them (far left, center) are hard to read as people.
The drones are small dark marks. They read as vague specks or birds rather than clear delta-wing shapes.
The window frame appears only as a thick vertical post on the left, so the window and balcony setup is a little ambiguous.

dawn.driver: Solar surpasses nuclear power globally for first time. Article URL: https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/09/29/solar-surpasses-nuclear-power-globally-for-first-time/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50131256 Points: 602 # Comments: 376
dawn.blurb: SOLAR OVERTAKES NUCLEAR ON THE GLOBAL GRID
dawn.summary: Sunlight now generates more of the world's electricity than nuclear power does, a milestone that panels on rooftops, deserts and farmland reached for the first time. Rivers are getting their own renewal, as dam removals across the northeastern United States bring fish back one small barrier at a time. In the ocean, researchers found that bleached corals bounce back within days when they touch a healthy neighbour.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Engineers moved a mirror one-sixteenth the width of a human hair, and NASA's Roman Space Telescope is now performing nearly 30% better than expected.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: Communities across the American Northeast are taking down small dams, and migrating fish are returning to streams they had been shut out of.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Thousands of devoted players keep BioWare's Neverwinter Nights alive with worlds and stories they build together, more than two decades after its release.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Solar has passed nuclear in global power generation for the first time, and bleached corals are recovering within days when placed next to healthy ones.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A rare pink French royal diamond, once found tucked inside an apple, goes on public display for the first time in a century.

copy_pick.why: Candidate 2 delivers the solar milestone in plain wire-service terms with a concrete image of rooftops, deserts and farmland, and it avoids the 'too' / 'Up in orbit' / 'Far overhead' transitions that echo the recent cards' 'Elsewhere' and 'Further out' handoffs.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. EXTREME CLOSE-UP filling the entire frame, in clear balanced midday daylight with confident, steady warmth. The setting is the foot of an old gray concrete reactor-plant apron, implied only by edges and reflections. A single huge sunflower fills the frame, pushing up through a jagged crack in the pale, weathered concrete slab. The slab fills the bottom edge and the left side, with chipped corners, rust-stained rebar stubs and tufts of fresh green grass in the fissure. The sunflower's face is the focal point. Its central disc is a perfect grid of tiny dark cobalt-and-teal photovoltaic cells, each with a thin silver busbar line and a gold highlight pixel, so the seed head reads as a solar panel. Around it, a thick ring of clear golden-yellow petals blazes with lighter yellow highlights and amber shadow pixels. Below the face, broad fresh-green leaves with bright lime edges and a thick, hairy green stalk rise from the crack. In the lower left, a shallow rain puddle on the concrete holds a small reflection of a curved cooling tower releasing a calm, pale plume. Beyond it the reflection shows rows of panels and a distant wind turbine. A second, much smaller sprout stands still and stunted in a hairline crack nearby, to show the contrast in growth. Soft, even daylight, no harsh shadows, with a palette of golden yellow, fresh green, warm concrete gray and small touches of cobalt.

minor: The puddle reflection shows the cooling tower, a wind turbine and solar panels all stacked in a small space. The perspective is a bit muddled and the tower looks cut off, but it reads as a reflection.
The rust-stained rebar stubs look like small brown twig-like bits scattered along the cracks, not clearly rebar.
The small sprout on the left is bright and healthy rather than stunted, so the intended contrast with the big sunflower is weaker.
The sunflower stalk and leaves emerge from the crack with a slightly unclear junction. The leaves overlap the stalk in a stylized way.
The solar-cell grid on the disc has uneven spacing and gold dots, but it reads clearly as a solar panel.
